summary: Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (professor in 2010), and Rissho University (professor in 2025).
Kenryu Tsuji was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Koyasan University (1926), Shuchiin University (1955), and Seizan College, and became professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenryū Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Otani University and is attested as professor emeritus at Hanazono University in 2014.

Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1975 and served as a professor there from circa 1999 to 2018.

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2004). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2014.

Kenyu Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley under teachers including Akira Hirakawa. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015).

Kevin Alan Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees at Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and was doctoral supervised by Bernard Faure, Chün-fang Yü, and Zhaohua Yang.

Khakyab Dorje was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Khenchen Tashi Özer, Tsuklak Nyinjé, Mingyur Wanggyel, and Sheja Künkhyen, and taught numerous students including Kalu Rinpoche.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He has served as a fellow and trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies and founded the Shan State Buddhist University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche. He chaired the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Khakyab Dorje and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Khenpo Gangshar and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1969–2023), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981–2023), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.

Khenpo Appey was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Drakgyab Lodrö and at Dzongsar Monastery. He served as director of Sakya College (1972–1985) and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
